**Summit County** is an urban county located in the northeast region of the U.S. state of Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 540,428,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-QF-3) making it the fourth-most populous county in Ohio. Its county seat and most populous city is Akron.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-GR6-4) The county was formed on March 3, 1840, from portions of Medina, Portage and Stark counties. It was named Summit County because the highest elevation on the Ohio and Erie Canal is in the county.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-5) Summit County is part of the Akron, OH Metropolitan Statistical Area, which is also included in the Cleveland-Akron-Canton, OH Combined Statistical Area.
According to the United States Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 419.38 square miles (1,086 km 2), of which 412.08 square miles (1,067 km 2) is land and 7.3 square miles (19 km 2) (1.7%) is water.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-GR1-6) The largest portion of Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in the northern part of the county. The southern border of the former Connecticut Western Reserve passes through the southern part of the county, leading to jogs in the east and west borders of the county.

**Summit County** is an urban county located in the northeast region of the U.S. state of Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 540,428,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-QF-3) making it the fourth-most populous county in Ohio. Its county seat and most populous city is Akron.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-GR6-4) The county was formed on March 3, 1840, from portions of Medina, Portage and Stark counties. It was named Summit County because the highest elevation on the Ohio and Erie Canal is in the county.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-5) Summit County is part of the Akron, OH Metropolitan Statistical Area, which is also included in the Cleveland-Akron-Canton, OH Combined Statistical Area.
According to the United States Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 419.38 square miles (1,086 km 2), of which 412.08 square miles (1,067 km 2) is land and 7.3 square miles (19 km 2) (1.7%) is water.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_County,_Ohio#cite_note-GR1-6) The largest portion of Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in the northern part of the county. The southern border of the former Connecticut Western Reserve passes through the southern part of the county, leading to jogs in the east and west borders of the county.

Akron consists of 21 neighborhoods, with an additional three that are unincorporated but recognized within the city. The neighborhoods of the city differ in design largely because of expansions such as town merging, annexation, housing construction in various time periods, and rubber era.
Maple Valley covers the west end of Copley Road, before reaching I-77. Spicertown falls under the blanket of University Park, this term is used frequently to describe the student-centered retail and residential area around East Exchange and Spicer streets, near the University of Akron. West Hill is roughly bounded by West Market Street on the north, West Exchange Street on the south, Downtown on the East, and Rhodes Avenue on the west. It features many stately older homes, particularly in the recently recognized Oakdale Historic District.
